sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** A defensive rotation is underway as Utilities and Consumer Defensive gain ground while Communication Services plunges, even as Energy retains its firm grip as the top momentum leader.

The US sector landscape on July 22, 2026, shows a distinct shift toward defensive and value-oriented groups. Energy remains the undisputed market leader with a momentum score of 0.93, anchoring a group of four "all-green" sectors that includes Real Estate, Healthcare, and Consumer Defensive. Meanwhile, high-beta and cyclical areas are showing signs of exhaustion, highlighted by a sharp drop in Communication Services and persistent weakness in Consumer Cyclical.

Defensive rotation is highlighted by Utilities and Consumer Defensive each climbing 2 spots in the rankings over the last five sessions. Conversely, Communication Services experienced a severe setback, falling 5 spots to rank 10. Technology remains a key momentum player at 0.67 (rank 2), but lacks the broad-based "all-green" designation held by more defensive peers.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Four out of 11 sectors maintain positive performance across all major timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD): Energy (0.93 momentum), Real Estate (0.67 momentum), Healthcare (0.55 momentum), and Consumer Defensive (0.42 momentum).
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy holds the number one YTD rank with a dominant momentum score of 0.933.
* **Tech and Real Estate Resilience:** Real Estate (rank 4) and Technology (rank 2) are tied as the second-strongest momentum leaders, both scoring 0.667.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Defensive Gainers:** Consumer Defensive (+2 spots to rank 6, momentum 0.42) and Utilities (+2 spots to rank 7, momentum 0.45) lead the 5-session improvements.
* **Communication Services Plunge:** Communication Services is the week's largest loser, dropping 5 spots to rank 10 with a lagging momentum score of 0.333.
* **Cyclical Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical remains anchored to the bottom of the board at rank 11, registering a negligible momentum score of 0.083.

## Divergences
* **Fragile Healthcare Trend:** Despite its "all-green" status, Healthcare shows a low agreement score of 0.44, signaling that its positive momentum (0.55, rank 9) is highly unstable.
* **Financials Disconnect:** Financials maintain a relatively strong momentum score of 0.583 (rank 8 YTD), yet the sector has begun to fade, losing 1 spot over the last five sessions.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive value and energy infrastructure dominate market leadership, while travel, internet tech, and solar face sharp weekly rotations out of favor.

Market breadth remains healthy with 30 of 144 groups holding all-green status across all timeframes. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.99 momentum) and REIT - Healthcare Facilities (0.90 momentum) lead the charge. We are observing a distinct rotation into consumer staples and defensive groups, with Tobacco (+16 spots) and Staffing & Employment Services (+11 spots) making major weekly rank gains, while Department Stores surged by 19 spots.

Conversely, growth and travel-related industries are fading quickly. Airlines and Internet Content & Information both plunged 19 spots, while Solar (-17 spots) and Internet Retail (-15 spots) experienced rapid deterioration. Additionally, early-warning signals show some established leaders like Railroads and Oil & Gas Midstream starting to slip in rank despite their high absolute momentum.

## Strength
* **Healthy Breadth:** 30 out of 144 industry groups maintain all-green status, showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons.
* **Top Momentum Anchors:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing dominates with a momentum score of 0.99 (YTD rank 3), followed closely by REIT - Healthcare Facilities (0.90 momentum, YTD rank 26) and Trucking (0.88 momentum, YTD rank 6).
* **Sustained Performers:** Healthcare Plans (0.85 momentum) and Staffing & Employment Services (0.85 momentum) continue to show sustained strength, holding top-36 ranks across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Department Stores led weekly gains, jumping 19 spots to rank 89 (0.62 momentum), followed by Tobacco (+16 spots to rank 38, 0.81 momentum) and Drug Manufacturers - Specialty & Generic (+15 spots to rank 95, 0.47 momentum).
* **Sharpest Decliners:** Airlines and Internet Content & Information both fell 19 spots (ranking 83 and 69, respectively), while Solar dropped 17 spots to rank 116 with a weak 0.30 momentum.
* **Bottom Laggards:** High-stress groups remain anchored at the bottom, led by Gambling (0.139 momentum, YTD rank 144), Advertising Agencies (0.099 momentum, YTD rank 143), and Airports & Air Services (0.079 momentum, YTD rank 137).

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum groups are starting to lose rank, including Railroads (0.84 momentum, -6 spots), Oil & Gas Midstream (0.76 momentum, -6 spots), and Consumer Electronics (0.78 momentum, -4 spots).
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Several low-momentum groups are jumping in rank, led by Specialty & Generic Drug Manufacturers (+15 spots, 0.47 momentum), Telecom Services (+11 spots, 0.43 momentum), and Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries (+10 spots, 0.48 momentum).
